$comment: CodeQL severity policy for agent-cli. Maps each CodeQL rule family to either 'block' (PR fails branch-protection required check on the CodeQL Analyze job) or 'advisory' (SARIF upload keeps showing it on the Security tab but does not block). Updated 2026-08-25 by the CodeQL fix planning team (qa-engineer + devops-engineer + software-architect + GPT-architect gpt-5.6-sol peer review).

policy_metadata.rationale: Block rules are real security or correctness bugs (CWE-classified where applicable). Advisory rules are quality/maintainability findings that do not pose an immediate risk; bulk-fix them in the next minor release rather than blocking each PR.
policy_metadata.enforcement_mechanism: Branch protection on main requires the CodeQL Analyze (javascript-typescript) job to pass before merge. The codeql.yml workflow itself does NOT fail-on-findings (so SARIF upload continues to the Security tab); enforcement is via branch-protection context.
policy_metadata.review_cadence: On every PR touching src/ or scripts/. Update this file in the same PR that adds a new CodeQL rule family (avoid silent enforcement gaps).
policy_metadata.false_positive_handling: Suppress with `// lgtm [rule-id]` and a one-line rationale in the code. The suppression does NOT remove the rule from this file — keep the block/advisory mapping authoritative here. Periodic review of `git grep 'lgtm\['` to ensure suppressions are still valid.
policy_metadata.new_rule_handling: If CodeQL adds a new rule family not listed here, it defaults to `block` (matches the principle of least surprise — better to surface than silently allow). Add the rule to the appropriate list in the same PR that suppresses its first finding.
